title: Finite-presentation data at an inverse limit

proof.text: Use the given limit cone identities c.w, Over.pullbackComp and its adjunction-mate counit identity to identify iterated pullbacks. Pullback.hom_ext and Over.w give the comparison equations. No existence theorem for a limit cone is needed.

For an object U, Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation (01ZM (1)) constructs a finite-presentation model V and its pullback comparison. Map V to the identity object T over the stage. The map after pullback to the limit is etale by Etale.of_comp and the comparison with U. Use Etale.exists_stage_of_inverseLimit (07RP) to descend this map, then compose with the etale structure map of the pulled-back identity object. Finite-presentation properties persist under pullback.

For a morphism between limit pullbacks, compose its underlying map with the target first projection. Scheme.exists_pullback_hom_of_isLimit (01ZM (2)) descends this map; form its Over morphism by pullback.lift. Check the required canonical-comparison equation on the two projections, using the private comparison_fst lemma. For equalities, compose the pullback equality with the target first projection and apply Scheme.exists_pullback_fst_comp_eq_of_isLimit (01ZM (3)); pullback.hom_ext gives equality in Over.

Apply the already-proved object clause to all finitely many vertices and use Finite.exists_le to move their models to a common stage. Apply finite_diagram_lift_of_models to descend only the generators and relations while keeping these models. Its object equalities give etale finite presentation of the resulting objects. At later stages use base-change instances for these properties, congrArg of the pullback map for relations, and naturality of the whiskered comparison isomorphism for every path.

Index the selected family by the subtype of the finite set B. Naturality of the inverse diagram comparison transports the limit covering to the canonical pullbacks of the stage family. Its arrows are locally of finite presentation by Etale.of_comp. Apply the proved finite_family_joint_surjectivity_stage. At each later stage the selected arrows are etale by cancellation against the etale structure maps of their source and target, and the helper supplies joint surjectivity.

split_report.summary: Rule 0: no slopmaster2 declaration states the item (grep by id, by 01ZM/07RP/07RR and by key words; 01ZM itself is closed Lean attached to thm-pd-spreading-out). The statement was vague ('descend', 'finite diagrams', 'sufficiently late stage of a descended diagram'); it is rewritten precisely as five assertions (objects, morphisms, equalities, finite diagrams with relations, coverings), with the same hypotheses and content. The blueprint proof (an affine reduction by generators and relations, gluing, and a compactness argument in the constructible topology, none citing a node) is replaced by Stacks Limits 01ZM (thm-pd-spreading-out, closed Lean), 07RP (lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale) and 07RR (lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective), whose proofs contain exactly those arguments; a finite family is reduced to one morphism through its finite coproduct, for which one new unsplit node (lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-lfp-qcqs) was needed. Stacks tags in the lead's brief: 07RP is descend-etale and 07RR descend-surjective (correct uses); 01ZR is descend-modules-finite-presentation and 07RL is Morphisms projective/quasi-projective, neither used.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 2-4 realize the first two paragraphs of the blueprint proof (affine finite-presentation calculation and the qcqs gluing giving the finite-diagram assertion), through 01ZM and 07RP, whose proofs carry out that reduction; steps 5-6 realize the third paragraph (the covering assertion; its constructible-topology compactness argument is the proof of 07RR via Limits 05F4), through 07RR applied to the morphism from the finite coproduct; step 1 is the bookkeeping the blueprint leaves implicit.
